body: Bahamut Lagoon is Square's Super Famicom tactical role-playing game about Byuu and the dragon squad resisting the Granbelos Empire. The world of Orelus consists of lands floating in the sky, giving the campaign a setting of isolated places connected by travel and conflict. Human characters fight in organised squads accompanied by dragons. The player develops both sides of that army, preparing its members between operations before moving them across a grid battlefield where the immediate clash can lead into a closer turn-based encounter.

Weapons, armour and other items can be fed to dragons to change their attributes and eventually their forms. Their preferences affect loyalty, making development involve more than simply offering the strongest spare equipment. During battle, the player gives general instructions while the dragons act with some independence. That separation lets a companion feel like a creature rather than another directly controlled soldier. Preparing its abilities and disposition matters because the next battle will ask it to use those qualities beyond the player's precise control.

Development began in 1994 with newer Square staff and changed from a conventional role-playing concept into a tactical design. Kazushige Nojima directed, Motomu Toriyama wrote the scenario and Noriko Matsueda composed the score. Designer Hitoshi Sasaki's memories of an aerial view over the Izu Peninsula helped inspire the floating landscape. Released only in Japan in 1996, the game joined intimate party relationships to a larger military campaign, with the dragons providing a second kind of attachment that the player could influence and develop between battles.
story_headings: An army travelling between floating lands
Feed the dragon for the next battle
A new team finds its own campaign
